benefits: A monthly scholarship of 992 Euros for a full month (calculated on a daily basis if you stay less than 23 days in a month)
Health insurance, accident and personal liability insurance
160 Euros travel stipend for travel within Germany / for the RISE meeting
Invitation to the three-day RISE Germany meeting in Heidelberg in July 2027
Canadian students on the Mitacs/DAAD combined scholarship receive 7,000 CAD from Mitacs plus DAAD insurance
eligibility: Currently enrolled in a bachelor's degree program at a university/college in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom or Ireland in biology, chemistry, computer science, physics, earth sciences or engineering (or a closely related field)
International students must prove that they study at a university/college located in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom or Ireland for more than 12 months by the application deadline
Must be an undergraduate who has completed at least 2 years of a degree program by the time of the internship placement
Must prove that undergraduate status is maintained after the internship has taken place
German citizenship holders are only eligible if they can prove they have been living outside of Germany for six years or more
requirements: The application process is completely online at the RISE Germany internship database
Register first for a DAAD ID to get access to the database
One motivation letter for each project applied to
A letter of reference from an academic who holds at least a PhD degree, uploaded online by the referee
Only complete applications are passed on to the internship providers
documents: Motivation letter (one per project applied to)
List of courses you will have completed by the time the internship begins (no longer than one page)
Transcript of Records (digital with university name/logo/student name and print date, or a copy of a certified hard copy)
Certificate of enrollment with university stamp, signature of an authorized person and expected date of graduation
Letter of reference on the official letterhead of the university with the referee's signature
selection_criteria: Undergraduates are ranked in order of academic performance, as indicated by their grade point average
Internship providers rank the applicants for their projects
Projects are ranked in order of demand, as indicated by the number of applications they have attracted
An alternating matching process assigns top projects their highest-priority available applicants and top students their preferred available projects
Providers may exclude undergraduates they feel are unsuited, though this rarely happens
coverage: Monthly scholarship of 992 Euros to help cover living expenses
Health, accident and personal liability insurance
application_method: Register first for a DAAD ID in the RISE Germany internship database
Search the internship offers and save an application for each project of interest
Upload the required documents: motivation letter per project, CV, list of courses, transcript and certificate of enrollment
Create a link for the professor so the letter of reference can be submitted online
Submit the complete application by 30 November 2026 (11:59 pm CET)
official.application_route: Fully online via the RISE Germany internship database: register for a DAAD ID, search projects, upload all documents and submit by 30 November 2026.
official.study_mode: Full-time research internship; virtual internships only where the individual offer explicitly mentions this option
official.citizenship_residency: Undergraduates enrolled at universities/colleges in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom or Ireland; German citizenship holders are only eligible if they have been living outside of Germany for six years or more
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are welcome provided they have studied at a university/college in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom or Ireland for more than 12 months by the application deadline, with the same application process
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Bachelor's degree program in biology, chemistry, computer science, physics, earth sciences or engineering (or a closely related field)
official.research_requirement: No separate research proposal is required; a tailored motivation letter is needed for each project, and the internship is supervised by a PhD student mentor or a researcher (only at universities of applied sciences)
official.duration: 3 months (minimum stay ten weeks, maximum stay 90 days); start between 15 May and 15 July 2027
official.description: RISE stands for Research Internships in Science and Engineering. RISE Germany offers undergraduate students from North American, British and Irish universities the opportunity to complete a summer research internship at top German universities and research institutions. RISE Germany is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office.
official.program_type: Government-funded research internship scholarship (German Federal Foreign Office)
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL or MOI score is published; the working language will be English and German language ability is not required unless the individual project description states otherwise

applicant_utility.summary: RISE Germany funds a three-month summer research internship in Germany with 992 EUR per month plus insurance and travel lump sums, and the summer 2027 round has a very short application window (15 October to 30 November 2026). Everything runs through the RISE Germany database, so the DAAD ID, a signed certificate of enrollment with an expected graduation date, and a PhD-holding referee all need to be lined up before the window opens. Placement is decided by an alternating match between provider rankings and applicant GPA, so strong grades plus a credible academic reference matter more here than in essay-heavy scholarships. Canadians should check whether they are routed through the Mitacs Globalink funding track, which pays 7,000 CAD instead of the DAAD stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Second- or third-year biology, chemistry, physics, computer science, earth sciences or engineering undergraduates at US, Canadian, UK or Irish universities who want mentored lab experience in Germany over one summer and will still be enrolled afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your expected graduation falls after the summer 2027 internship - spring/summer 2027 graduates are not eligible this round
Register for your DAAD ID before 15 October and test the portal login on a desktop, since mobile use is limited
Agree with a professor holding a PhD who will upload the reference on official university letterhead before 15 December 2026
Request the certificate of enrollment early and insist on the expected graduation date, university stamp and authorized signature
Draft a one-page list of courses you will have completed by the internship start date
Arrange a European IBAN bank account for the stipend and check visa rules if your stay will exceed 90 days
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete files: anything still missing when the window closes means the application is never forwarded to the internship providers
Reference-letter failures - letters from companies are rejected outright, a referee without a PhD disqualifies the letter, and a missing signature or letterhead voids it
Losing undergraduate status after the internship, which removes the work-permit basis for the placement
Generic motivation letters: each project receives its own letter, and providers rank applicants partly on how well the letter fits their specific project
Applying through a single-field filter: offers are filed under one discipline even when they span biology and chemistry, so narrow searches hide suitable projects
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing is not funded - the supervisor only helps you find a dorm room or shared flat you pay for yourself - and living costs beyond the 992 EUR monthly stipend, visa fees for stays over 90 days, and flights beyond the international lump sum and the 160 EUR domestic travel stipend remain on the student.
document_audit: The transcript must show university name/logo, student name and a print date; a certified hard-copy scan is accepted even with an 'issued to student' stamp

The certificate of enrollment needs the university stamp, an authorized signature and a prospective/anticipated/expected graduation date - a plain registrar screenshot without the date is the classic failure
One motivation letter per project, uploaded inside the portal, with no word or page limit
The reference letter must be submitted by the professor through the generated web link; a letter emailed by the student is not accepted
A lab supervisor's letter is only accepted if that internship took place in a university setting and lasted at least two months
alerts: You cannot apply to both RISE Germany and RISE Professional in the same cycle - you must choose one
German citizens only qualify if they have lived outside Germany for six years or more, and must state this in the CV
Withdrawing after acceptance causes real inconvenience for DAAD and the host institution, so only apply to projects you genuinely want
Canadian students are largely routed through Mitacs Globalink (7,000 CAD plus DAAD insurance) rather than the DAAD stipend - confirm which funding route applies before applying
Virtual internships carry different scholarship rates and exist only where the offer explicitly says so
No individual feedback on the application is given, by email or phone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online only: create a DAAD ID in the RISE Germany database, save one application per project with all six documents, generate the referee link, submit by 30 November 2026; DAAD completeness-checks the file, providers rank applicants 14-25 January 2027, and placements are announced around February/March 2027.
